summary: Changed three local Android plugin forks to apply legacy Kotlin Gradle Plugin imperatively only when AGP built-in Kotlin is disabled. Strengthened the two-mode debug gate to fail on Flutter's KGP migration warning. Debug and signed Release builds passed in legacy and built-in modes without that warning; generated release APKs verify with APK Signature Scheme v2. No ADB/device was used.

checks.name: Regression gate rejects the known Flutter KGP warning
checks.observation: Test-first run failed as expected because Flutter emitted its KGP warning for flutter_background, flutter_webrtc and livekit_client. After the plugin scripts were updated, the same gate passed both modes and rejected no KGP warning.

checks.name: Legacy and AGP built-in Kotlin Debug matrix
checks.observation: Legacy mode built with flutter build apk --debug --no-pub; built-in mode built with :app:assembleDebug -Pandroid.builtInKotlin=true. Neither build emitted Flutter's KGP compatibility warning.

checks.name: Signed legacy split-ABI Release matrix
checks.command: cd desktop && JAVA_HOME=<JDK 17> flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi --no-pub
checks.observation: Produced armeabi-v7a (30 MB), arm64-v8a (38 MB) and x86_64 (43 MB) signed APKs. apksigner verified APK Signature Scheme v2 for each.

checks.name: Signed AGP built-in Kotlin universal Release
checks.observation: Universal signed APK (107 MB) built successfully; apksigner verified APK Signature Scheme v2. Flutter's KGP compatibility warning was absent.

limitations: Remote CI has not yet run against this change.
No Android device, ADB, installation, or runtime acceptance was performed.
The default remains android.builtInKotlin=false; this change validates compatibility but does not change the default build mode.
remaining: Run the Android CI workflow after push. Device/runtime checks remain separate and require ADB; they were intentionally not attempted.
